channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: UK Signals ‘Different View’ From Trump on Russia Sanctions
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s government disagrees with US President Donald Trump’s approach to sanctions on Russia, a key UK minister said, signaling a growing divergence between the allies over the Ukraine war.
item.dc:creator: Alex Morales

item.title: Four Canadian Soldiers Killed in Military Base Fire, Carney Says
item.description: Four Canadian soldiers were killed and dozens more were “seriously wounded” after a fire tore through an army base in Alberta Saturday, Prime Minister Mark Carney said.
item.dc:creator: Sybilla Gross

item.title: Trump Says DC Golf Course Project Moving Ahead Despite Suit
item.description: President Donald Trump formally announced the creation of a new pro-level golf course in Washington, DC, on Sunday, despite legal challenges, distress over downed trees and local ire over the loss of an affordable and family-accessible golf spot.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: US Chamber of Commerce Endorses Paxton in Texas Senate Race
item.description: The nation’s largest business lobby said it is endorsing Ken Paxton, the Trump-endorsed Republican candidate for a Senate seat from Texas.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: US Ukraine Disagree on Starshield, Riots in France, Watching Wall Street
item.description: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by “All Things Considered” NPR Host and “American Pope” Author Scott Detrow, US Senate Candidate and New Hampshire Rep. Chris Pappas, PIMCO EVP & Market Strategist Tony Crescenzi, Political Analyst & “The Creativity Con” Author Thomas Frank, Condé Nast Traveler Senior Features Editor Megan Spurrell, Texas Rep. Marc Veasey, Freeland and Cook Political Report Senate and Governors Editor Jessica Taylor. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zimbabwe Ruling Party Picks Mnangagwa as Candidate for 2030 Vote
item.description: Zimbabwe’s ruling party has picked President Emmerson Mnangagwa as its candidate for the 2030 national presidential election, a vote that will be conducted in parliament under the country’s revised electoral system.
item.dc:creator: Godfrey Marawanyika

item.title: Trump Endorses Netanyahu for Reelection as Israeli Leader
item.description: US President Donald Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following months of increasing strain between the two leaders.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Senate Control Moves Toward a Toss-Up
item.description: Bloomberg congressional reporter Erik Wasson and Cook Political Report Senate and governors editor Jessica Taylor tell Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump’s weak approval ratings are expanding the midterm battlefield, giving Democrats opportunities in states that normally favor Republicans. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, they say Democrats have multiple paths to Senate control, while a potential Democratic Congress could set up major fights with the White House over spending, the debt ceiling and foreign policy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: France Struggles to Contain Fallout From Nationwide Protests
item.description: France is grappling with the aftermath of a weekend of widespread protests that descended into clashes between police and demonstrators and sparked some of the worst street violence the country has seen in years, with looting and landmarks set on fire. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Debt Boom Faces Bond Market Reality Check
item.description: PIMCO Market Strategist and Portfolio Manager Tony Crescenzi tells Bloomberg This Weekend that rising US interest costs and the selloff in CoreWeave debt show how bond investors are imposing greater discipline on borrowers, particularly companies with less certain cash flows. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Crescenzi says divided government could be supportive for markets after the midterm elections and argues the AI investment cycle still has a long way to run. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zelenskyy Says Discussing New Talks With Witkoff, Kushner
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he’s holding talks Sunday with US President Donald Trump’s envoys with a view to arranging a new rounds of peace meetings as early as this week.
item.dc:creator: Daryna Krasnolutska, Volodymyr Verbianyi and Olesia Safronova

item.title: Thirty Seconds in Texas Costs $12,000 as Politics Dominates TV
item.description: Buying a 30-second television ad in Harlingen, Texas, typically cost political candidates less than $500 two years ago. These days the spots are going for the price of a serviceable used car in the small city near the Mexican border.
item.dc:creator: Joe Lovinger

item.title: Starshield Dispute Exposes US Ukraine Divide
item.description: Bloomberg News National Security Team Leader Wendy Benjaminson tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Ukraine uses SpaceX’s Starshield and Starlink systems for critical military operations, as questions remain over what caused recent restrictions and whether they were deliberate. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Benjamin says the dispute comes as Republican criticism grows over President Donald Trump’s approach to Russia and Ukraine ahead of the midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Pappas Says New Hampshire Race Is Not in the Bag
item.description: Rep. Chris Pappas, the Democratic nominee for US Senate in New Hampshire, tells Bloomberg This Weekend that his race against former Republican Sen. John E. Sununu remains highly competitive despite Democratic optimism heading into the midterm elections. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Pappas says Democrats must keep reaching independent and ticket-splitting voters while focusing on the economy, cost of living and President Donald Trump’s leadership. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: France Faces Unrest Over Rising Living Costs
item.description: Bloomberg News Reporter Gaspard Sebag tells Bloomberg This Weekend that nationwide protests over the cost of living and public services have descended into violence in parts of France, adding to pressure on President Emmanuel Macron’s government. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Sebag explains how France’s fiscal constraints leave the government with limited room to address protesters’ economic concerns as the country approaches a presidential election. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Faces GOP Backlash Over Russia Sanctions
item.description: Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Jeff Mason tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump’s decision to waive new sanctions on Russia is drawing criticism from Republicans and Democrats while adding strain to the US relationship with Ukraine. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Mason explains how Trump’s push to lower diesel prices ahead of the midterms is shaping his Russia policy and raising questions about whether the strategy can deliver relief for voters in time. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: France Struggles to Contain Fallout From Nationwide Protests
item.description: France is grappling with the aftermath of a weekend of widespread protests that descended into clashes between police and demonstrators and sparked some of the country’s worst street violence in years, with looting and landmarks set on fire.
item.dc:creator: Gaspard Sebag

item.title: Russia, Ukraine Keep Up Attacks as Zelenskyy Renews Appeal to US
item.description: Russia and Ukraine continued to trade attacks overnight as Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he was ready for fresh talks with the US and renewed an appeal for Washington to put pressure on Moscow.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Saudi Helicopter Crashes Near Yemen as Houthi War Rages
item.description: Two people died when a Saudi Arabian reconnaissance helicopter crashed near the border with war-torn Yemen, the first fatalities of their kind reported by the kingdom since the latest flare-up in its battle against Houthi rebels.
item.dc:creator: Sara Gharaibeh

item.title: Trump Faces Widening GOP Backlash Over Russia Sanctions Waiver
item.description: Republican lawmakers, including some of the president’s strongest allies on Capitol Hill, blasted Donald Trump for waiving new tariffs and sanctions on Russia, prompting the president to defend himself against members of his own party.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres and Jeff Mason
